$comment: External golden ephemeris reference for the science gate. Generated by scripts/generate-ephemeris.mjs from the NASA/JPL Horizons API.
sourceName: NASA/JPL Horizons System (VECTORS ephemeris, heliocentric ecliptic J2000)

units.epoch: Julian Date (TDB); calendar dates are UT

sanityChecks.description: rows are validated against the published radial and speed range before being recorded

note: JPL Horizons was not reachable from this machine, so no external vectors were recorded (reason: Error: failed to fetch https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api?format=text&COMMAND='399'&OBJ_DATA='NO'&MAKE_EPHEM='YES'&EPHEM_TYPE='VECTORS'&CENTER='500%4010'&START_TIME='2000-01-01'&STOP_TIME='2000-01-02'&STEP_SIZE='1d'&VEC_TABLE='2'&REF_PLANE='ECLIPTIC'&REF_SYSTEM='J2000'&OUT_UNITS='KM-S': TypeError: fetch failed). NO numbers were invented. Run `npm run generate:ephemeris` on a host with network access: it requests VECTORS tables with CENTER='500@10' (Sun centre), REF_PLANE=ECLIPTIC, REF_SYSTEM=J2000, OUT_UNITS=KM-S for Mercury, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Moon at 2000-01-01, 2026-09-29, 2035-01-01, 2049-12-31, validates every row, and writes them here.
